title: What Comes After AGI?
lede: A Google DeepMind essay treats intelligence as a continuum and sketches how AI might move from human-level AGI to superintelligence, and how to track that progress.

points: It defines ASI as systems that consistently beat large expert groups on long tasks across nearly all domains, faster and cheaper.
Growth in hardware, algorithmic efficiency and investment is estimated to multiply effective compute at least tenfold a year.
The authors call the resulting commoditisation of cognitive work cognitive industrialization.
Four routes to ASI are named, including scaling models and data, paradigm shifts and multi-agent coordination.
Bottlenecks include running out of training data, diminishing returns on scale and physical limits on power and chips.

points.text: The top comment rejects the premise, calling claims that AGI is near propaganda and arguing LLMs are a communications technology.
Several note the goalposts have moved: what the essay calls ASI is roughly what AGI meant before LLMs.
Commenters split on the compute extrapolations: one says investment cannot keep compounding, a reply says real capability would fund itself.
Others doubt intelligence can be measured precisely enough to place anything on such a continuum.
